body:
> Where is "supports opaque ranges" defined?

Whoops, forgot to define that 🤦. Added it to the "APIs for the text control selections" section. Let me know if you'd prefer it placed elsewhere as I wasn't sure where the best spot for it was.

What is supposed to happen to `OpaqueRange`s when the text control element becomes `display: none`? Should the ranges survive a `display:none` roundtrip, or are they disconnected?
And does creating a range (`createValueRange()`) on a `display:none` element even make sense?
I think `display: none` shouldn't impact a range? No other range is impacted by styling, why would this one be?

(speaking with an implementers hat on) it has implications to implementations if the frame gets destroyed (and re-created), if destroying the frame implicitly destroys the internal text node that is referred to in the opaque range. 
My interpretation would be that it's implicitly expected that the range survives, but I wonder if this should be written somewhere explicitly.
I see. I think we should make sure that the specification doesn't have such assumptions anywhere and then just add explicit test coverage.
Good call on `display:none`. Added WPT coverage for it.

AI feedback Reviewed at 5e71356; line numbers refer to `source` at that commit. `lint.sh` passes. The new row in the input-type summary table matches the `setSelectionRange()` row, all new cross-references resolve, and the imported DOM anchors match what whatwg/dom#1404 generates. **Blockers** - **The opaque range internal container can get out of sync with the value** (L63754–63756). It is described as "a `Text` node whose data is the element's relevant value". That leaves open whether it is a single persistent node per element (the ranges' boundary points depend on that), what its node document is, and what cloning does. Its data only changes through the *opaque range replacement steps*, and every hook only runs while the element currently *supports opaque ranges*. The `type` change algorithm (L51353–51418) has no hook at all, and neither does *change an `input` element's value on behalf of the user* (autofill, L56688). Two examples: - ``, `r = input.createValueRange(2, 7)`, `input.type = "url"`: sanitization makes the value `"Hello"`, but `r` stays at 2–7 and the container keeps `" Hello"`. - On an empty text input: `input.createValueRange(0, 0)`, `input.type = "hidden"`, `input.value = "abc"`, `input.type = "text"`, `input.setRangeText("X", 3, 3)`. This runs *replace data* at offset 3 on a container whose data is still `""`, so `setRangeText()` throws `"IndexSizeError"` after already changing the value. Consider making it an explicit associated `Text` node (for example, null until the first `createValueRange()` call, then created from the relevant value with the element's node document). Then remove the *supports opaque ranges* conditions from the hooks, add hooks to the `type` change and autofill algorithms, and define what a `type` change does to existing ranges. - **`createValueRange()` is missing from the per-state bookkeeping sections** (L51598–55099). The summary table says it is non-normative. The normative "apply" and "do not apply" lists are in each state's bookkeeping section, and none of them mention `createValueRange()`, so "does not apply" in step 1 of `createValueRange()` (L63812) currently has no normative meaning. Please add it to the "apply" lists for Text/Search, Telephone, URL, and Password, and to the "do not apply" lists for the other 17 states. - **Tests:** web-platform-tests/wpt#63041 makes `OpaqueRange-disconnect.html` and `OpaqueRange-auto-disconnect.html` non-tentative. But `disconnect()` was removed in 5e71356, and nothing in this PR resets ranges on removal, adoption, or `type` change; the test even expects a reset when going from `text` to `search`. Consider keeping those tests tentative until the behavior is specified. **Suggestions** - Consider dropping steps 1–4 of the *opaque range replacement steps* (L63771–63793) and the *set of associated OpaqueRanges*. - Because the container's data is the relevant value, each range's boundary-point offsets equal its value offsets once *replace data* has run. - So after step 6 you can set each range's exposed start and end offsets to its start and end offsets. Iterate over each opaque range whose start node is the container, as DOM does for live ranges. - This keeps exposed offsets as discussed in #11478 and removes the duplicated adjustment rules. It also avoids a set that only grows: nothing removes ranges from it, and its entries keep them alive. - Consider defining "the edit's code unit offset" and the removed and inserted counts in terms of the relevant value (L56653, L59007). - For `textarea`, user edits change the raw value, while ranges count API-value code units. The raw value can contain U+000D (CR) characters, as in the `demo.value = "A\r\nB"` example. - With raw-value offsets, the *code unit substring* step would read past the end of the value, and *replace data* would throw. - It would also help to say how a single user action that changes several separate parts of the value is handled. - Consider running the full replacement in the `textarea` *children changed steps* (L59037) only when the API value changes, as the reset algorithm does. It currently checks for a raw-value change but passes API-value lengths. So changing the child text from `"a\r\nb"` to `"a\nb"` collapses every range even though the API value is unchanged. - Consider capturing the old value in a variable in the hooks for the `input` `value` content attribute (L51153), `input` reset (L51202), `textarea` reset (L59048), and the `textarea` children changed steps. They refer to "the old value" or "the previous API value" without defining it. - Consider moving the new sentence for the `value` content attribute (L51153) inside the `` that holds the requirement it refers to. As it stands, the developer edition shows "this operation" with nothing before it. - Consider using "method steps are:" and `this` for `createValueRange()` (L63807). The neighbouring algorithms use the older form, but new text generally uses the modern one. Step 1 could also check *supports opaque ranges* instead of the applies table, so the two lists of types can't drift apart. - Consider confirming that `createValueRange()` handles its arguments differently from the other selection APIs on purpose: - `setRangeText()` and `setSelectionRange()` throw `"InvalidStateError"` when they don't apply, and clamp out-of-range offsets. `setSelectionRange()` collapses a backwards range to `end`. - `createValueRange()` throws `"NotSupportedError"` when it doesn't apply, throws `"IndexSizeError"` for out-of-range offsets, and collapses to `start`. - Consider `concept-…` `data-x` values for the imported DOM concepts (L3284), for example `concept-OpaqueRange-exposed-start-offset`. HTML uses the `dom-` prefix for IDL members. - Consider exporting *supports opaque ranges*: w3c/csswg-drafts#13929 links it from DOM, where it no longer exists. CSSOM View (w3c/csswg-drafts#12904) and the Highlight API (#13929) also need to get from an `OpaqueRange` to its element, for geometry and for their "not in this document" check. Consider exporting a way to do that, for example "the element whose opaque range internal container is the range's start node". - Consider moving the new definitions and `createValueRange()` (L63742–63841) after the `SelectionMode` text (L63843), or into their own subsection. Right now they sit between `setRangeText()`'s algorithm and the enumeration that goes with it. - Consider saying in the developer intro (L63283) that the returned range updates as the value changes, since that's its main point. **Nits** - L49947–49949: "the `setRangeText()` and `setSelectionRange()`, and `createValueRange()` methods" should be "the `setRangeText()`, `setSelectionRange()`, and `createValueRange()` methods". - L49765, L58941: use `OpaqueRange` in the IDL, like `NodeList` and `SelectionMode`. - L51417: stray blank line in the `type` change algorithm. - L59328: an unchanged step was rewrapped and is now 102 columns; L63829 is also over 100. - L63672: `max(0, …)` isn't needed, because the earlier `"IndexSizeError"` check ensures start ≤ end. The preserve branch later computes the same value as `old length`, which could be moved up and reused. - L3284: `data-lt` isn't needed, since the reference uses `data-x`. Consider splitting this entry over several lines like the `ProcessingInstruction` one. - L63803: the note can go; code units are already UTF-16. - L59330: "If this changes the element's API value" could be "If the element's API value is different from oldAPIValue", matching the next step. - PR description: - The commit message could name the web-facing change (for example, "Add createValueRange() to input and textarea") instead of "This PR…", and reference #11478. - The HTML-AAM item can probably be marked N/A, and the MDN item is still open. - You could add yourself to the Acknowledgments.
